title: The Books of the Changes
kicker: The Recursive I Ching · a history in books, one book per chapter
description: How a Western Zhou diviner's handbook became a classic, a cosmology, an imperial exam text, a Jesuit proof, a Victorian scripture and a German wisdom book, and what each of those books changed in the text.
intro:
This course is the family tree of the I Ching read as a story, one book per chapter, oldest first. The same chapters are the nodes of the [genealogy](../viewers/genealogy-tree.html) and the dots on the [timeline](../viewers/timeline.html).

Four changes run through it. First, words were attached to numbers: a diviner's handbook, the Zhouyi. Then the Ten Wings wrapped those words in a cosmology of yin, yang and trigrams, and a Han emperor fixed the wrapped text as a classic. After that, readers split between those who looked for the order of the world in the figures (images and numbers) and those who looked for a teaching in the words (meanings and principles); the second line became the exam text of the empire and the text the first Europeans translated. In the last century scholars pulled the layers apart again, and tombs gave back copies older than the canon.

Each chapter has the same four parts: what the book is, what it changed in the text, the record (where each claim comes from), and, when the book is here, a link to read it. The marks say how sure each claim is: ✔ checked in the cited source, ○ indirect, ◆ contested, ◇ from memory and still to check. A few claims are still ◇, each waiting on a source that has not been opened yet.
